headline: The whole of Georgia lost power for nine hours

sources.title: Georgia plunges into darkness as rare nationwide blackout hits
Georgia hit by nationwide power outage

chunks.text: The lights {{went out}} across the whole of Georgia at about 00:10 on July 24. Tbilisi, Kutaisi and the [[breakaway]] region of Abkhazia all lost power [[at once]]. Georgian State Electrosystem, the national [[grid]] operator, said an emergency [[shutdown]] had caused it and that supply would return [[in stages]]. Power was fully [[restored]] at about 09:30, more than nine hours later, but the official cause is still unknown.

verbs.correct: To stop shining or working, as a light does
verbs.wrong: To be officially approved or passed

chunks.text: A national grid works as one machine, with [[supply and demand]] held in balance second by second. If a large plant or line fails, automatic protection {{kicks in}} and disconnects equipment to [[prevent]] damage, and the loss can {{knock out}} the rest of the system in seconds. In April 2025 a shutdown of the Kavkasioni [[transmission line]] left about 90 percent of [[consumers]] without power.

verbs.correct: To start to work or take effect
verbs.wrong: To create a lot of noise or fuss
To reduce a price by a small amount

chunks.text: The energy ministry in Abkhazia blamed a system failure at the Enguri [[hydropower]] plant, which supplies both Abkhazia and territory held by Georgia's central government. Tbilisi did not comment on that [[account]]. The grid operator said the exact causes were still being established. It also {{called on}} news organizations to [[rely on]] official information, saying false claims were [[circulating]]. No explanation has yet been [[confirmed]].

verbs.correct: To formally ask someone to do something
verbs.wrong: To cancel something that was planned

chunks.text: Several Tbilisi metro trains stopped inside tunnels on the night's last services, and the Tbilisi Transport Company said every passenger {{got out}} safely. Georgian Water and Power said its [[pumping stations]] {{shut down}} automatically, putting water supply [[at risk]] in Tbilisi and Rustavi, though the company said the night passed with [[minimal]] problems. Power {{came back on}} area by area, reaching parts of the capital and Kutaisi by 02:09. The rest of the country spent the night in the dark.

tf.s: The lights went out across the whole of Georgia at about 00:10 on July 24.
tf.why: The lights went out across the whole of Georgia at about 00:10 on July 24, and Tbilisi, Kutaisi and Abkhazia all lost power at once.

tf.s: The energy ministry in Abkhazia blamed a system failure at the Kavkasioni transmission line.
tf.why: The energy ministry in Abkhazia blamed a system failure at the Enguri hydropower plant. The Kavkasioni transmission line was the line involved in a separate shutdown in April 2025.

tf.s: The Tbilisi Transport Company said every passenger got out safely.
tf.why: Several Tbilisi metro trains stopped inside tunnels, and the Tbilisi Transport Company said every passenger got out safely.

tf.s: Georgian Water and Power said its pumping stations shut down automatically.
tf.why: Georgian Water and Power said its pumping stations shut down automatically, putting water supply at risk in Tbilisi and Rustavi.

tf.s: Power came back on across the whole country by 02:09.
tf.why: Power came back on area by area, reaching parts of the capital and Kutaisi by 02:09, but the rest of the country spent the night in the dark.

tf.s: Officials have confirmed exactly what caused the blackout.
tf.why: The grid operator said the exact causes were still being established, and no explanation has yet been confirmed.

mainIdea.s: An entire country lost power at once for more than nine hours after an emergency shutdown. Electricity returned in stages, and the official cause has still not been confirmed.
mainIdea.why: The blackout hit every region just after midnight, and supply came back area by area. The operator says the causes are still being established.

mainIdea.s: A whole nation spent nine hours without electricity after a failure at a hydropower plant. The grid operator confirmed the plant caused it and promised to install new equipment.
mainIdea.why: Close, but only one region blamed the plant. The national operator has not confirmed any cause, and no new equipment was promised.

mainIdea.s: Metro trains stopped inside tunnels and water pumps failed during a long night in the dark. Officials now plan to rebuild the capital's aging underground and water systems.
mainIdea.why: The trains and pumps show the blackout's effects. Nothing in the story says those systems will be rebuilt.
